summary_rationale: Creative Newtech is a profitable, fast-growing technology distributor whose profit has not yet been shown to turn into durable cash, so the record supports a conditional grade. Earnings growth is real and audited: total income rose from ₹370.70 Cr in FY19 to ₹2,717.51 Cr in FY26 (33% a year) and PAT from ₹5.85 Cr to ₹70.29 Cr. Margins are thin: FY26 EBITDA was ₹103.95 Cr, 3.8% of total income, and Market Entry earns a 3.8% segment margin against 33.2% for Brand, so 14% of revenue carries 59% of segment result. Cash conversion is the weak point: operating cash flow was negative in seven of eight years (cumulative −₹328 Cr against ₹241 Cr of profit), −₹271.88 Cr in FY26, then +₹351.24 Cr in H1 FY27, about 84% of it from payables and advances that the CFO calls unsustainable. Growth is funded by banks, suppliers and ₹171 Cr of TReDS vendor finance; borrowings rose from ₹72 Cr to ₹324 Cr in FY26 and interest cover is about 5x (Crisil BBB+/Stable). Management is dependable on one-year guidance but has missed its multi-year cash, margin and licence aspirations. The Honeywell licence, whose renewal management has dated three ways, supplies roughly half of EBITDA, and the largest customer is about 25% of revenue. The weakest assumption in any favourable reading is that ₹683 Cr of September 2026 payables and customer advances is recurring working capital rather than quarter-end timing; if it reverses, the FY26 funding strain returns.
